claims.claim: Reviewers note that vehicles like the Seamoth can get stuck or caught in the terrain due to bugs.

citations.review_text: Cool concept and beautiful game, but janky, unintuitive, and obtuse at times. If you are hoping for some sort of guide or for a game that will hold your game, this isn't it. The game has a story, but you are very much encouraged to decipher it yourself. I didn't mind the loose story or the open-ended exploration. What kind of soured the experience was the bugs which almost make me want to not recommend the game. It's been 8 years and the amount of unfixed bugs is astounding; a problem like Seamoths getting caught in terrain is still a problem all these years later. I am glad I got it on sale as I wouldn't recommend it at regular price. Fun game, but frustrating at times.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience constant survival mechanics involving the regular consumption of food and water.

citations.review_text: This is a very stupid game. Possibly the worst game I have ever played. I spent 11 hours on it according to my Steam client, so I believe I gave it a fair shot. First of all, there are absolutely no rails on this game at all. You are dropped into the middle of the ocean and you have no idea what any of your long or short term objectives are, other than to not die. So you swim around picking up various items to build other items. But you need to drink fresh water and eat food regularly or else you die. The food and water requirement is constant and never ending and it is a chore. Not fun. Games are supposed to be fun. This is not. 11 hours into the game and I still do not know what my overall goal is supposed to me. Imagine watching a streaming series and you are 11 episodes into it and you still do not know what the main conflict and plot is supposed to be. I am astounded by the positive reviews of this game.

Subnautica makes you think through events to survive. It is at your pace. Swimming endlessly in the water enjoyable. The knife if you flash it during the day time you get ate. So do not keep it in your hand. You fabricate items as you pick up substances and debris out in the ocean. You can have fish raw or cooked. Fish provide bottled water.  Creepy vines withe yellow flowers that you have to have that get you radiated. Makes you sentient. I am 66 and using the controller to maintain fine motor skills for that Texas test for driving now added. Pleasurable way to do and under the sea intriguing, a bit of danger and gorgeous to view.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that resource gathering and searching for specific materials can become tedious and grindy.

citations.review_text:
Thalassophobia Simulator

If you've not heard of this game by now you must have been living under a rock, as this game defined the underwater survival genre — and it did it horrifyingly so.

This game is an absolute work of art. It has spectacular visuals and an abundance of replayability. It certainly does not disappoint; from its captivating exploration to its below-the-surface horror aspects, it is just outright amazing.

The progression of equipment and upgrades is nice, but it can be slightly tedious if you're missing one particular material and have to swim all the way back to where you came from to get it.

The atmosphere on Planet 4546b is just perfect. From the safe shallows to... well, not the safe shallows, there is beauty around every corner.

The sound design is phenomenal and the commentary is unforgettable. Literally unforgettable. Like, it's stuck in my head. I can hear it in my sleep. Help me.

As for the story? There isn't much direction for progression, but do get ready to be invested. It's great.

If I were the protagonist I would've peed my pants so many times, but you wouldn't have known this because I would be underwater.

A really fun and beautiful game, I would highly recommend you play it if you haven't! The experience of this game is worth full price, but honestly wait until it goes on offer as it does so frequently.

[i]Beware the Reaper Leviathan. If you can hear it, it has already seen you.[/i] 9.2/10
Good, not great. The ambience of Subnautica is really good at the start, but the open underwater world gets pretty tedious and grindy. Still think it's worth it on a sale.

The idea is great, but it gets tedious with most of your time spent swimming and searching rather than building or problem solving.  If you liked Red Dead Redemption 2 but wished you had to spend more time fishing, riding between towns, and skinning animals, but less time in combat and story this is your game.

cohorts.summary: Mid-game players praise the strong overall performance and Steam Deck compatibility while noting minor bugs and repetitive survival loops.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running very well on the Steam Deck.

citations.review_text:
What a game. I got completely sucked in every time I booted it up.
I did very nearly stop playing for a while after a botched attempt to get to the Lost River, but I got over myself and devoured the rest of the game. I even got emotional at the end - that's not happened to me with a game before.
It also runs really well on the Steam Deck.
I did encounter a couple of bugs - resources that had spawned below the floor, mostly. I floated through the roof of my Cyclops twice, those were definitely brown-trouser moments, but I save often, so I just closed + reopened and all was well.

I've immediately become nostalgic for the game and will likely need to replay it.

One of my favorite games of all time!
I loved this game. I played it all the way through on Steamdeck.
Tips:
1. I managed to get my full size sub down into the lowest levels (use those external cameras and channel your inner Austin Powers in a golf cart, lol). It was great because it would constantly re-charge the batteries over the lava and I used it as a mobile home base for the moth and the mech suit.
2. My other tip is building a second base in the lower levels, but it makes you do that a little higher than the lava level so I used it to stash loot.
3. You can grow plants in your sub in planters and stash extra loot in duffle bags.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention encountering small bugs that can be annoying while noting that the game runs extremely well overall.

citations.review_text:
Easily the best game in its genre. It has the full package of a great told story, well crafted world, interesting traversal through the world and enough semi-horror to keep you on your toes. I found a lot of small bugs (not insects) that were pretty annoying, but not enough to detract from the experience.  Ran extremely well!

9/10
This game might be my favorite survival game, Light on the survival until the deep parts and really beautiful. I had some issues but overall the game ran fine.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience annoyance with certain survival mechanics and resource gathering loops.

citations.review_text:
I have been waiting to play this game for some time. I went in knowing as little information as possible which I think is the best way to experience the first playthrough. While survival game mechanics in general can be annoying to deal with at times, I felt this game was quite well-balanced in that respect. The world is so thoughtfully designed, and I wish I could re-experience the joy of entering a new biome for the first time again. This game gave me jump scares, filled me with dread and tension, encouraged my curiousity to learn about the world, and ended with a sense of accomplishment. 

This is a game where you crash land on a water planet and must figure out how to survive. To say any more would be to take away from the joy of exploration and mystery that this game brings. 

Highly recommend!!
7/10 really. Not into "picking up and smashing rocks all the time" loop.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight the frustration of missing auto-save functionality leading to lost progress.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks an auto-save feature, which can result in losing progress.

citations.review_text: As an enjoyer of the survival, base-building genre, the game itself is a blast, but the inability to run the game without crashing every 20 minutes is absolutely horrendous. Most of my time was spent AFK in the main menu, and the rest of the time was spent catching up to where I last crashed at. It's my first time and I wanted to play on hardcore, but without the ability to consistently save it's an absolute nightmare. I will not be playing more of Subnautica and I will not be playing or buying Subnautica 2. Googling "Why does subnautica" with the first two autofill results showing "keep crashing" and "2 keep crashing" is my sign.
Doesn't have auto save, you could lose everything in a few clicks.
